doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: 'Putting It Together', his first Blue Note date as leader
summary: Elvin calls this trio album a favorite, with Garrison's compositions, Farrell, and 'Keiko's Birthday March'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Okay back to the chronology. We are back at the end of ’67. You’ve put your group together; you’ve got your trio. I believe we talked about “Putting It Together” .So this is the first date as a leader on Blue Note.
And you, in a recent interview, singled this out as one of your favorites.
Would you like to talk about why?

Why? Because you only have to listen to it. Jimmy Garrison’s compositions and Joe Farrell who’s like a wizard with his reed. He could play any kind of reed instrument, double reed, whatever. They were just great musicians and it was fun to play together. We had a lot of fun and we enjoyed each other. That’s the way it was. That’s where I played the “Keiko’s Birthday March” the cadence in front is a long 2-4 that we used to play in the marching band.
